g.text: Intro to Mech Interp - Full Walkthrough
TransformerLens, ActivationCache, hooks, induction heads, logit attribution, ablation.
TransformerLens = HookedTransformer with proper access to every activation.
ActivationCache = dict-of-tensors with all intermediate states.
Visualize the (query, key) attention matrix per head.
Three shapes to look for: current-token, previous-token, first-token.
Induction heads (the whole point of TransformerLens)
A famous circuit: 2 heads that let the model predict repeated sequences.
Detect them with a 'repeated random tokens' probe.
At each position i, attends to position i-1.
Effect: token embeddings shift forward by 1 in the residual stream.
So after this head, resid at pos 5 (2nd A) contains info about pos 4 (E).
At the target position, forms Q from current residual.
K at each past position: prev-token head wrote 'preceded-by-A' info at pos 1 (B).
Current Q matches K at pos 1: attention spike from pos 5 to pos 1.
V at pos 1 is 'B'. OV writes B into resid at pos 5. Model predicts B.
How to detect: repeated random tokens, look for the INDUCTION STRIPE

Split each head into two 'circuits': OV (what to copy) and QK (where to attend).
K-composition: layer-1 head's keys are LINEAR functions of layer-0 head's writes.
OV circuit: what does the head COPY?
For any token x on which head attends,
the head writes attn · (x @ W_V @ W_O)
If diagonal is high → head copies
QK circuit: WHERE does the head attend?

For a possible K-composition path from L0 head h0 to L1 head h1:
numerator = ||W_OV[h0] @ W_K[h1]||_F ← Frobenius norm of product
score close to 1 = product is large relative to input norms → strong composition.
